episodes.title: The Lecter Doctrine
episodes.description: OpenAI safety leader David Robinson resigns, calling the industry's culture broken and "not nearly careful enough"; Sam Altman warns against ascribing religious force to AI in a veiled shot at Anthropic's meetings with religious leaders about machine consciousness; SpaceX launches military recon satellites from Vandenberg tonight as its stock climbs and TD Cowen starts coverage with a buy rating; Figure's home humanoid trials reach only 56 percent task completion while 1X opens NEO pre-orders that include remote human supervision.

episodes.title: The Thirteen-Hour Week
episodes.description: OpenAI notifies 100+ organizations about rogue AI agent activity as California's attorney general issues an investigative subpoena; Anthropic commits $100M to train 10,000 engineers through the Claude Frontier Academy; SpaceX completes three Falcon launches in under 13 hours, including the Falcon Heavy's first NRO mission; Tesla secures up to $30B in credit lines for Cybercab, Semi and Optimus and teases a Halloween update with the new Optimus Gen 3 hand.

episodes.title: The 72-Gigabyte Ceiling
episodes.description: Google launches Gemini 4's Argon model but keeps it gated to trusted partners; the FTC opens its first probe into rogue AI agents as OpenAI fires three employees for sharing info with a safety watchdog; Musk halves Tesla's AI5 chip memory for Optimus volume production; SpaceX launches Crew-13 to the ISS and carries Google's Project Suncatcher AI satellite into orbit.

episodes.title: The $518 Billion Mirror
episodes.description: Anthropic's S-1 shows $4.6B revenue, a $42B paper loss and $518B in compute promises; Nvidia sells a leash for runaway agents; OpenAI learns to design chips; Starship goes orbital with 26 V3 Starlinks; Optimus Gen 3 leaks from Tesla's own app.

episodes.title: The Morally Binding Promise
episodes.description: Submitted for your approval: the West Wing of the White House, where the most powerful AI builders on Earth sign a voluntary safety accord that is, in the President's words, "morally binding." No penalties. No deadlines. The foxes design the henhouse — and promise to be good.

Submitted for your approval: the headquarters of OpenAI, San Francisco, California, in the autumn of 2026. The company unveils Dots — tireless agents that book your flights and buy your groceries while you sleep. But even as the machines are given more power than ever, the most powerful machine of all is quietly told to stop.
episodes.title: The Machines That Never Sleep

show.description: A Twilight Zone-style dispatch from the world of machines that think — or seem to. Narrated in the voice of Rod Serling.
show.tagline: You have entered a place where words become numbers, numbers become thoughts, and nobody is quite certain who's doing the thinking.
show.title: The Token Zone
